captions.instagram:
F-1, OPT, H-1B: which federal tax form you file depends on your tax residency, not the visa name alone.

✔️ F-1 and J-1 students are generally nonresidents for their first 5 calendar years: Form 1040-NR if you had income, plus Form 8843.
✔️ H-1B workers who meet the substantial presence test (31 days this year, 183 weighted days over 3 years) are generally residents: Form 1040.
✔️ The year you arrive or switch can be a dual-status year.
✔️ Some popular tax apps don't support Form 1040-NR. Check before you pay.

Tax information only, not immigration advice. We prepare both. Student package: Form 1040-NR + 8843 + tax-treaty check, $99 federal ($129 with one state return). H-1B residents filing Form 1040: our standard 1040 pricing. Federal plus NJ and NY returns. Book a call to start. Not available for CA, CT, MD or OR state returns.

sources.fact: Substantial presence test: 31 days in the current year and 183 days over 3 years (all current + 1/3 prior + 1/6 second prior); days as an exempt individual (F, J, M, Q students) are not counted (read 2026-10-24)
Students generally become residents after 5 calendar years (exempt-individual period); Form 8843 Part III >5 years rule (read 2026-10-24)
H-1B who meets the substantial presence test is treated as a U.S. resident and reports worldwide income on Form 1040; dual-status aliens file a special return (read 2026-10-24)
Dual-status: status changes during the year, usually the year of arrival or departure (Topic 851, read 2026-10-24)
TurboTax: 'TurboTax doesn't support IRS Form 1040-NR' (Intuit help article, read 2026-10-24)
